gaps.sentence: Little ___ anyone realise how close the firm was to insolvency.
gaps.explanation: "Little did anyone realise" = nobody realised — emphatic inversion with do-support.

gaps.sentence: So rapid ___ the spread of the fire that the building was lost.
gaps.explanation: 'So rapid was the spread that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than the rumours started.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been signed than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Only when the last guest had left ___ she sit down.
gaps.explanation: 'Only when … had left did she sit down' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ refunds be given after this date.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances will refunds be given' — inverted modal passive.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ the tenders been opened when the leak was traced to the press office.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly had … been opened when' — past perfect passive with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ the defendant change his statement.
gaps.explanation: Not once has he changed… — emphatic negative with present perfect.
